documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 02/11/2025

Type 1 diabetes, nearly four years. Readings reviewed from his meter; overnight values steady, lunch is still the weak spot. No severe hypoglycemia, no ED visits. A1c drawn.

Regimen unchanged: glargine 16 units at bedtime, lispro sliding scale with meals. Next visit in 6 months.

Allergies: NKDA.
Endocrinology

documents.body: Hi - need refills on strips and needles again. And the college disability office wants a letter that I have type 1 diabetes so I can have my meter and snacks during exams. Can you write one?

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 26 y/o with Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes and T1DM. His roommate told him this morning his eyes were yellow. Got back last night from five days camping, where food was limited and meals were irregular - ate very little some days. A bit tired since getting home, which he puts down to not drinking enough and poor sleep in the tent. No belly pain, nausea, vomiting, weight loss, itch or dark urine. No recent illness, no alcohol or drugs, no new meds or supplements. Sugars ran a little high on the trip, no lows. Spells before this: exam periods in 2022 and early 2023 and after his appendectomy in July 2023. He also remembers one earlier in college after a few all-nighters and skipped meals that went away on its own.

Meds: glargine 16 u qhs, lispro scale, valacyclovir prn. NKDA. PSH: lap appendectomy 2023.
FH: older brother with Gilbert syndrome, paternal cousin with Dubin-Johnson.

O: vitals normal, BMI 22. Well, no distress, alert and oriented. Scleral icterus; skin not jaundiced. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly, liver span normal to percussion. No spider angiomas, palmar erythema or ascites. Heart and lungs normal. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
Icteric spell after several days of poor intake, in known Gilbert syndrome (with Dubin-Johnson). Hepatic panel with fractionation and CBC to confirm the usual unconjugated pattern. Fluids, regular meals, sleep. No further workup unless the labs look different from his past spells.

documents.title: Bilirubin results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bilirubin 2.6, almost all indirect; liver enzymes normal; hemoglobin 14, normal. Same Gilbert-type spell you've had before after not eating much. No treatment needed. Pack more food next trip!

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request for glargine pens, endocrinology prescriber unreachable before the weekend and pt down to his last pen. One-month bridge of glargine 16 units at bedtime approved by PCP; pt to have endocrinology send ongoing refills.

documents.title: Rooming
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual. Meds verified from pt's pens and bottle: glargine 16 units nightly, lispro per scale with meals, valacyclovir prn. NKDA. PHQ-9: 3. Flu and covid today.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

26 y/o. Last semester of coursework planned for this year. Feels well.

Interval: one yellow spell in May after a camping trip, labs as usual for his Gilbert syndrome, cleared within a week. Endocrinology in February, regimen unchanged. One cold sore this summer, valacyclovir. He did see the optometrist last winter, but no report reached us; he's booked again for November and will ask them to send it.

Meds as rooming. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. No icterus. Mouth clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular; lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Feet: skin intact, sensation normal to monofilament, pulses 2+. Affect normal.

A/P
1. T1DM on basal-bolus insulin per endocrinology - A1c, CMP, microalbumin, lipids, TSH today. Optometry report requested after his November exam.
2. Gilbert / Dubin-Johnson - nothing new.
3. Recurrent HSV-1 labialis - valacyclovir prn.
4. Flu and 2025-26 covid given. PHQ-9 3.
Spring follow-up to touch base on diabetes.

documents.title: Labs from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All reassuring: kidney numbers and urine protein normal, thyroid normal, cholesterol fine, blood counts normal. A1c about the same as last year. Bilirubin slightly up as always.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic eye exam letter, outside optometry practice. Exam date 11/13/2025.
Vision 20/20 right, 20/20 left. Anterior segments quiet. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy in either eye, no macular edema.
Return in 12 months.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual PA for glargine pens expired with the new plan year. Renewal submitted with diagnosis and current regimen (16 units at bedtime). Approved 1/14 through 1/2027. Pharmacy notified.

documents.body: You said to come in this spring for a diabetes check. Do you have anything in late April? Afternoons are best, I have class in the mornings.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Spring diabetes check. Sees endocrinology roughly twice a year; he skipped his fall visit with a busy semester and has one coming up in the summer. Same doses: glargine 16 units at bedtime, lispro by his scale. Checks 3-4 times a day. A couple of mild lows after long soccer games, treated himself. No yellow spells since last May. One cold sore over the winter, settled with valacyclovir. Optometry report from November came in: no retinopathy.

Meds: glargine, lispro, valacyclovir prn. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Starting a summer soccer league.

O: vitals as charted. Well. No icterus. Lips clear. Heart regular; lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: skin intact, sensation normal, pulses palpable.

A/P
1. T1DM - A1c, CMP and urine microalbumin today, copy to endocrinology. Discussed summer soccer: carry fast sugar, check before and after games, drink plenty in the heat.
2. Gilbert / Dubin-Johnson - quiet.
3. Recurrent HSV-1 - valacyclovir prn, refills current.
Annual physical in September.

documents.title: Results from Wednesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c is in your usual range. Kidney function and urine protein normal. Bilirubin mildly high as always. I sent a copy to endocrinology for your summer visit. See you in September.

documents.title: Valacyclovir refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request, valacyclovir 500 mg BID prn. Last fill 11/2025. Renewed per standing plan, 30 tabs, 2 refills.

events.reason: Lightheadedness and nausea after soccer in the heat

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 07/11/2026

CC: lightheaded, dizzy and nauseated after soccer.

HPI: 27-year-old man with type 1 diabetes, Gilbert syndrome and Dubin-Johnson syndrome (most recent jaundice spell May 2025). Played about three hours at a summer soccer tournament in direct sun with no real breaks. Drank water through the day but ate little. Over the last hour felt lightheaded, dizzy and queasy and teammates brought him in.

Meds: insulin glargine 16 units at bedtime, insulin lispro sliding scale, valacyclovir prn. PSH: laparoscopic appendectomy. NKDA. No tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Triage vitals: T 39.5 C (103.1 F), HR 110, BP 100/60, RR 22, SpO2 98% on room air.
Exam: skin cool and moist. Fatigued, oriented x3. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs: Na 135, K 4.2, Cl 100, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 90.

ED course: moved to a cool room, ice packs and fans. Normal saline 2 L IV. Glucose rechecked by fingerstick and stayed in range with oral intake. Repeat vitals T 37.6 C, HR 86, BP 114/70. Nausea and dizziness gone, walking without symptoms, tolerating fluids.

Diagnoses: heat exhaustion; dehydration.
Disposition: discharged home with a friend. Rest and fluids for 24-48 hours, no sports until fully recovered, check glucose more often for the next day. Follow up with primary care as needed.

[Received 08/11/2026, filed]

documents.title: Went to the ER Saturday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to tell you I ended up in the ER Saturday after a soccer tournament - got dizzy and sick to my stomach in the heat. They said heat exhaustion and dehydration, gave me two bags of fluid and sent me home. Feeling normal now. Sugars were fine the whole time.

documents.title: Re: Went to the ER Saturday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're feeling back to normal. Take it easy for a few more days, build back slowly, and on hot days take real breaks in the shade with fluids and some salt and carbs, checking your sugar before and after. If dizziness or nausea come back, call us. We'll get the ER record for your chart.

documents.body: Is my September physical still on? I can't remember the date.

documents.title: Re: Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Yes - Thursday September 17 at 8:40 am. Come fasting if you can, and bring your meter.
